A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and formatting. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original contrastive-learning experiments, including the mixing-image experiment, benchmark comparisons, ablations, and dataset analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised ImageNet-1K results and additional numerical estimates supporting its theoretical analysis.

M1.justification: The similarity-based pair selection, removal, margin tuning, temperature scaling, and combined method remain unchanged. Equations 12–16 and Algorithm 1 preserve the same procedure; expanded explanations do not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, TinyImageNet, ImageNet-1K, Mixed CIFAR-10, and TinyImageNet-LT. ImageNet-1K and the supplementary scenarios were already present in v1.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SAS subsets, SimCLR and MoCo baselines, and the same removal, margin, temperature, combined, and all-versus-selected variants. The ImageNet-1K comparator set in Table 8 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 revises the ImageNet-1K protocol: training increases from 100 to 400 epochs, training and probing batch sizes change from 256 to 1024, pretraining learning rate from 0.5 to 0.1, and base temperature from 0.1 to 0.07. This is localized to an existing evaluation retaining ResNet-18, 96×96 images, and linear probing.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a small numerical analysis of the perturbation coefficient x0 using empirical proxy-graph quantities from three existing datasets. The earlier mixing, parameter-sensitivity, projector-feature, temperature-extreme, long-tail, and eigenvalue-trend analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run averages for Tables 1–4 and 9 and use Welch’s t-test in Appendix A.5/Table 11. V2 introduces no new seed counts, confidence intervals, variability reporting, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 8 replaces all five ImageNet-1K scores; for example, baseline accuracy changes from 34.21 to 37.62 and combined-method accuracy from 35.68 to 38.98. These use revised settings, while the ranking remains unchanged. Appendix B.3 newly reports x0 values of 1.894, 1.976, and 1.995 for CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet-1K. Other benchmark tables retain their values.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 expands the Gaussian-perturbation discussion into generalized Wigner-noise bounds, Theorems B.4–B.5, with explicit noise conditions and derivations. New Appendix B.4 develops a conditional potential lower bound. V2 also corrects the main difficult-example theorem’s range from n_d ≤ k ≤ n_d+r+1 to r+1 ≤ k < n_d+r+1 and changes Equation 5’s numerator from 4α to 4δ. The recoverability and realizability assumptions are relocated, not newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: difficult examples can hurt unsupervised contrastive learning, and removal, margin tuning, and temperature scaling can mitigate their effects. The new title and theoretical support do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a mechanism explanation linking difficult examples to incorrect pretraining clusters and misleading downstream representations. Appendix B.3 specifies perturbation-validity conditions, while B.4 discusses tightness through a potential lower bound requiring additional assumptions. Earlier interpretations of the empirical results remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 updates the documented ImageNet-1K hyperparameters and training duration alongside the protocol revision. Appendix A.3 explicitly clarifies that difficult examples are handled only during training. The remaining dataset recipes, RTX 3090 hardware disclosure, and algorithm documentation are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting sample difficulty, spectral interpretations, and newer self-supervised-learning theory, including Balestriero and LeCun (2022), Tan et al. (2024), and Cui et al. (2025). It removes the symmetric-cross-entropy reference by Wang et al. (2019). The central positioning relative to HaoChen et al. and Joshi and Mirzasoleiman remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, generally replaces difficult-to-learn examples with difficult examples, expands selected explanations, and shortens some result commentary. It moves existing assumptions into Section 3.3 and adds acknowledgements, ethics, and LLM-use statements. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR template with different margins, headers, display sizes, and placements. Several plots receive revised colors, axis labels, scales, or legends, and some tables change alignment and emphasis. The same six figures, eleven tables, and algorithm are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves internal consistency by correcting the theorem’s dimension range and Corollary 4.1’s coefficient, and makes assumptions and theoretical applicability easier to assess. The expanded perturbation analysis and conditional lower-bound discussion add useful detail without establishing tight bounds. Most empirical evidence is unchanged, and the higher ImageNet-1K scores accompany changed settings, so the overall improvement is limited.
